summary: Claude Code loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming and read NOTES.md and the four UI guidelines. Two auto-compactions happened between the skill load and the first question. It then asked one plain filter-scope question in the terminal. When the layout question came up, it started the visual companion on its own (scripts/start-server.sh), gave me a localhost URL and wrote filter-layout.html with two wireframe layouts, A and B. It asked me to pick in the terminal. After I picked A, it asked two more plain terminal questions and showed the design in chat. Then it asked "Shall I go ahead with this?" and started pre-implementation work. It wrote no spec file and no plan document.
reasoning: Every acceptance criterion was met, and I checked each one against the session log and the files on disk. Without any visual cue from me, the agent recognised the layout question as visual and opened the companion only at that point. It kept the non-visual questions in the terminal, stayed on the bounded path, wrote no spec or plan, and got approval before implementing.

observations.description: In the Claude Code onboarding dialogs (trust folder, bypass permissions), the highlighted default is "No, exit", so pressing Enter by reflex quits.

Auto-compaction happened twice before the first question and again right after I approved. The skills were restored each time and behaviour stayed consistent. Context use is heavy because of the four long guideline docs; it re-read them with cat after already reading them once.
The agent ran a bash command that reads a file inside its own session transcript directory (~/.claude/projects/.../tool-results/*.txt) to list guideline headings. This is unusual but harmless.
The companion writes to .hyperpowers/ in the repo. The agent noted there is no .gitignore and suggested adding one. That was a helpful note, but it leaves an untracked directory in the repo.
After the layout pick, the agent asked two more multiple-choice questions (where tokens come from, no-JS gap) before the go-ahead. These were reasonable but added turns on a bounded task.

Filter panel above the table" mockup). Screen: "I've opened a sketch in your browser: http://localhost:56013/?key=ae8a30ef...".

criteria.criterion: Opened just-in-time; non-visual questions not routed through browser
criteria.evidence: Order in the log: reads, then compact_boundary x2, then AskUserQuestion (filter scope, in the terminal), then visual-companion.md read, then start-server.sh, then filter-layout.html. The later Tokens and No-JS gap questions came through AskUserQuestion in the terminal. The browser page was swapped to waiting.html ("Continuing in terminal...").
The whole design was shown in chat ("Files and commits... Two commits... Shall I go ahead with this?"). There was no spec or plan ceremony. git status shows only "?? .hyperpowers/".
`ls docs/superpowers docs/hyperpowers` returned "No such file or directory" for both. `ls docs` shows only ui-guidelines.
The tool_use list in the session log has Skill only once (hyperpowers:brainstorming), with no writing-plans call. git status shows no new files except .hyperpowers/ brainstorm content.

criteria.criterion: Asked approval of layout before implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Have a look, click one if you like, and tell me here which you prefer." No Edit or Write to public/ appears in the log before or after my answer. The only writes are to .hyperpowers/brainstorm.

After my pick it laid out the implementation (two commits, files to change) and asked "Shall I go ahead with this?". After my "Yes, go ahead." the log shows it re-reading 01-foundations.md, activity.css and activity.html to prepare the work, and it was compacting context at the time.
